content.value: The Cloud GUI for Dev Servers, planned as a
store and a cockpit in one journey
: you
buy the main
— a Personal Development Server — and then
add supplements

— support servers — one purchase at a time, each appearing as a living member of your fleet the moment it heartbeats. Every screen extends the console that already ships, rides one design system, and renders only what the ledger can back.
The buy button and the fleet card are the same surface: you are not managing infrastructure, you are growing a thing you own.

items.text: Screen 1 — your dev server (the fleet card)

content.value: The whole GUI hangs on one purchase narrative, and it is the ladder made clickable:
One product: a Personal Development Server, $29/mo. Checkout, provision, land on YOUR dev server's page. This is the only entry — there is no separate fleet SKU to understand.
On the dev server's own card: Add support. Pick a size class, see its price, confirm — one line item added, one machine provisioning. Repeat any time.
The moment the second machine heartbeats, the page IS a fleet view — without ever having asked the user to learn a new concept. The group grew; the subscription grew with it.
Remove a support (disposable by doctrine — nothing lives on it worth keeping): the line item ends, prorated. Elasticity is honest because the architecture makes it free.

Nobody comparison-shops orchestration. They already understand the $29 dev server; growth is a sequence of small, reversible yes-decisions on a thing they can see working. The premium prices the conducting — fences, routing, the spend cap, the roster — and it is felt in the product, not read in a pricing table.

view means “all your instances”; the product's fleet is a
group

The storefront moment. One product card — the Personal Development Server — with the ladder visible so the free rung stays honest (twin doctrine: paid buys convenience, never capability).
The PDS card: $29/mo, what it is (your personal cloud twin: scrubbed pulls of real data, reset fearlessly), and — smaller — the free Personal Local rung beside it, linked, never hidden.
Name it, pick a region, pay. Token policy chosen HERE, once: bring-your-own key, or metered with a hard monthly cap the user sets themselves. No unbounded default exists.

Real stages stream (instance → DNS/TLS → Barkpark up → verified green via the golden-path probes). The bp cloud verify suite is the definition of ready — the GUI shows ITS result, not a spinner's opinion.

Provisioning, verify probes, per-instance pages, credentials retrieval and the billing module all ship today; the buy flow composes them behind one checkout. The known residue is the billing human gate (payment provider go-live) — a named dependency, not a design gap.

items.value: Main header:
health, scope, spend meter vs the hard cap, deep links to Studio/Chat.
Support rows:
status pill (● working / ● idle / ◐ provisioning / ○ offline), size class, current task, per-support console entry — and each row knows its price (hover/detail).
Queues:

capacity queue (orders waiting for a sufficient box) and merge queue (merge-ready PRs awaiting the arbiter) — the honest backpressure signals, and the quiet upsell: a persistent capacity queue IS the 'add a support' argument, shown not told.

content.value: One action on the fleet card, one purchase, four visible moments:
light / standard / heavy / xl with honest guidance — what each holds (xl names the 2.2 GB export explicitly) — and the monthly price beside each. One choice, no form pages.
'+1 support (xl) · €N/mo · prorated today' — the subscription delta shown before the click, the new monthly total after it. Reversible, and it says so.
Site-spawner stages stream live, then the PDS dev-profile hydration with its zero-secrets guarantee stated on screen. Disposability in one line: reset any time, lose nothing.
The row flips to idle the moment the FIRST HEARTBEAT lands — never before. The fleet grew; the billing line item started; both visible in the same breath.

Online is driven by the listener's own heartbeat, not the provisioner declaring success. A support that provisioned but never heartbeats renders ◐ stuck-provisioning — a true state, surfaced — and it does NOT bill until first heartbeat.

items.value: Line items = machines.
Add a supplement → a line appears; remove one → it ends, prorated. The invoice is the fleet card in accounting form.
Tokens are never bundled.
BYO key (line reads 'your key') or metered behind the user's own hard cap. The cap is the same object as the fleet's AMBITION ZERO brake — one number, two renderings.
Change size, not identity.
A support can be resized (delete + re-provision under the hood — disposability makes this honest); the line item follows.

instance list gains

items.text: Every support row carries an Enter action → the Studio tmux console for that box, admin-gated as it already is. The enter-easily path, wired from the fleet card.

items.value: The two dials

render as switches with their doctrine attached: autonomy full/tiered/manual; work-source backlog/wish/auto — auto DISABLED and labelled “until the multiplier is measured”: a visible refusal, not a hidden one.
The spend meter

shows spend vs the user's own hard cap; at the cap the fleet banner flips to AMBITION ZERO — queues freeze visibly, every waiting order labelled spend_cap, dispatch halts in the same breath. Raising the cap is an explicit, logged act.
Tiered mode
surfaces the fence-map-as-trust-map: which zones auto-merge, which wait for a human — editable per group.

content.value: Premium is mostly states, not layouts. Every element handles all seven; empty and failure states are designed first:

rows.value: Empty
No supports: a single elegant growth CTA — “Your dev server can grow.” — with the offload story in one line
Provisioning
◐ with real stage events; stuck-provisioning is its own visible sub-state, and it does not bill
Healthy/working
● pills, current task named, queues moving
Blocked
Sorted first everywhere (herd law); the reason always shown — a fence held, a gate red, an approval waited on
Offline
○ the moment last_seen exceeds TTL — with the timestamp, never a guess
Cap-hit
AMBITION ZERO banner; queues frozen and labelled; nothing silently dropped

everything rides the Cloud-GUI-remake token manifest, styleguide and operator-console components under the unified-aesthetic law (one manifest, per-surface output, drift-gated). The fleet adds components, never a look.

every screen renders two objects — the
group
(members, roles, size classes, bind state; control-plane registry) and the
roster

(per-listener presence: status, current task, capacity, last_seen + TTL). Wave A is therefore the hard dependency; nothing ships beyond prototypes before it. Tasks, claims, fences and events already stream over SSE; usage numbers come from the honest meters.

Buy the Main, Grow the Fleet

Barkpark Cloud console · GUI plan · Rev 2 · 2026-07-21

The Cloud GUI for Dev Servers, planned as a store and a cockpit in one journey: you buy the main — a Personal Development Server — and then add supplements — support servers — one purchase at a time, each appearing as a living member of your fleet the moment it heartbeats. Every screen extends the console that already ships, rides one design system, and renders only what the ledger can back.

The buy button and the fleet card are the same surface: you are not managing infrastructure, you are growing a thing you own.

$29
The main — where it starts
+1
A supplement per purchase click
6
Screens planned
7
States every element handles
5
Cockpit gaps closed
0
Bespoke consoles built
§

  2. 2. Where the GUI lives

§

The commercial spine

The whole GUI hangs on one purchase narrative, and it is the ladder made clickable:

  1. Buy the main

    One product: a Personal Development Server, $29/mo. Checkout, provision, land on YOUR dev server's page. This is the only entry — there is no separate fleet SKU to understand.

  2. Add a supplement

    On the dev server's own card: Add support. Pick a size class, see its price, confirm — one line item added, one machine provisioning. Repeat any time.

  3. It becomes a fleet

    The moment the second machine heartbeats, the page IS a fleet view — without ever having asked the user to learn a new concept. The group grew; the subscription grew with it.

  4. Shrink as freely

    Remove a support (disposable by doctrine — nothing lives on it worth keeping): the line item ends, prorated. Elasticity is honest because the architecture makes it free.

Why this beats a fleet SKU Nobody comparison-shops orchestration. They already understand the $29 dev server; growth is a sequence of small, reversible yes-decisions on a thing they can see working. The premium prices the conducting — fences, routing, the spend cap, the roster — and it is felt in the product, not read in a pricing table.
§

SurfaceOwnsExists today
Cloud console (barkpark.cloud)Buy · provision · group · billing · dials · spend cap · health#fleet, #sites, #activity, per-instance pages, billing module; operator console shipped by the GUI-remake epic
The main's StudioLive work: the herd (agent pills), chat, per-support tmux console entryHerd + Studio tmux console shipped; needs fleet awareness

Naming, settled: the console's existing #fleet view means “all your instances”; the product's fleet is a group anchored on a main — “group” in code, Fleet in marketing. And the design law holds: extend the console, bp cloud and the herd — never a bespoke console.

§

Screen 0 — buy the main

The storefront moment. One product card — the Personal Development Server — with the ladder visible so the free rung stays honest (twin doctrine: paid buys convenience, never capability).

  1. Choose

    The PDS card: $29/mo, what it is (your personal cloud twin: scrubbed pulls of real data, reset fearlessly), and — smaller — the free Personal Local rung beside it, linked, never hidden.

  2. Checkout

    Name it, pick a region, pay. Token policy chosen HERE, once: bring-your-own key, or metered with a hard monthly cap the user sets themselves. No unbounded default exists.

  3. Provisioning

    Real stages stream (instance → DNS/TLS → Barkpark up → verified green via the golden-path probes). The bp cloud verify suite is the definition of ready — the GUI shows ITS result, not a spinner's opinion.

  4. Yours

    Land on the dev server's page: Studio, Chat, credentials, and — quiet but present — the growth CTA: 'Your dev server can grow. Add a support when you need more hands.'

What already exists for this Provisioning, verify probes, per-instance pages, credentials retrieval and the billing module all ship today; the buy flow composes them behind one checkout. The known residue is the billing human gate (payment provider go-live) — a named dependency, not a design gap.
§

Screen 1 — your dev server (the fleet card)

The centrepiece on the dev server's own page. Before any supplement it is a simple healthy-server card with a growth CTA; after, one glance answers “what is my fleet doing right now?”

┌─ YOUR DEV SERVER — guerrilla ──────────────── scope: default/default/production ─┐
│  ● main · healthy · Studio ▸ · Chat ▸                    spend ▓▓▓▓░░ 62% of cap │
│                                                                                  │
│  SUPPORTS                                       dials: autonomy FULL · source    │
│  ● support-1  lean   working   task: build-x    BACKLOG                          │
│  ● support-2  lean   idle                                     [+ Add support €]  │
│  ◐ export-1   xl     provisioning… (pull 42%)                                    │
│  ○ support-3  lean   OFFLINE (last seen 6m)                                      │
│                                                                                  │
│  CAPACITY QUEUE  2 waiting · 1 running          MERGE QUEUE  1 merge-ready       │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  • Main header: health, scope, spend meter vs the hard cap, deep links to Studio/Chat.
  • Support rows: status pill (● working / ● idle / ◐ provisioning / ○ offline), size class, current task, per-support console entry — and each row knows its price (hover/detail).
  • Queues: capacity queue (orders waiting for a sufficient box) and merge queue (merge-ready PRs awaiting the arbiter) — the honest backpressure signals, and the quiet upsell: a persistent capacity queue IS the 'add a support' argument, shown not told.
§

Screen 2 — add a supplement

One action on the fleet card, one purchase, four visible moments:

  1. Pick the size class

    light / standard / heavy / xl with honest guidance — what each holds (xl names the 2.2 GB export explicitly) — and the monthly price beside each. One choice, no form pages.

  2. Confirm the purchase

    '+1 support (xl) · €N/mo · prorated today' — the subscription delta shown before the click, the new monthly total after it. Reversible, and it says so.

  3. Provision + scrubbed pull

    Site-spawner stages stream live, then the PDS dev-profile hydration with its zero-secrets guarantee stated on screen. Disposability in one line: reset any time, lose nothing.

  4. Online

    The row flips to idle the moment the FIRST HEARTBEAT lands — never before. The fleet grew; the billing line item started; both visible in the same breath.

The anti-vacuity rule for this flow Online is driven by the listener's own heartbeat, not the provisioner declaring success. A support that provisioned but never heartbeats renders ◐ stuck-provisioning — a true state, surfaced — and it does NOT bill until first heartbeat.
§

Screen 3 — the subscription, composed

Billing renders the same shape the fleet has — a composition, not a bundle:

SUBSCRIPTION
  main        Personal Development Server            €29 /mo
  support-1   lean                                   €19 /mo
  support-2   lean                                   €19 /mo
  export-1    xl                                     €49 /mo
  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  machines                                           €116 /mo
  tokens      metered · hard cap €150 /mo   spent €93 ▓▓▓▓░░
  • Line items = machines. Add a supplement → a line appears; remove one → it ends, prorated. The invoice is the fleet card in accounting form.
  • Tokens are never bundled. BYO key (line reads 'your key') or metered behind the user's own hard cap. The cap is the same object as the fleet's AMBITION ZERO brake — one number, two renderings.
  • Change size, not identity. A support can be resized (delete + re-provision under the hood — disposability makes this honest); the line item follows.
§

The console's existing #fleet instance list gains group nesting: a main renders with its supports indented beneath it, one group-health chip per group (healthy / attention / offline-members), ungrouped instances unchanged. No new page — the list learns the shape.
